doubts.question: Sir, how do we resolve the boundary condition when finding orthogonal trajectories for r^n = a^n cos(n theta)?

messages.message: Sir, how do we resolve the boundary condition when finding orthogonal trajectories for r^n = a^n cos(n theta)?

Take logarithm on both sides first: n ln(r) = n ln(a) + ln(cos(n theta)). Differentiate with respect to theta and replace dr/dtheta with -r^2 (dtheta/dr). You will obtain r^n = c^n sin(n theta). See lecture note 4.2.
Understood sir, the logarithm substitution simplifies the product rule. Thank you so much!
